name: M.Sc. (Horticulture) Floriculture and Landscaping
duration_note: Coursework is normally completed in the first year and thesis research in the second. The ICAR BSMA framework totals 70 credits, with 30 credits for thesis research. Some universities title the degree Floriculture and Landscape Architecture.
regulator: ICAR (Broad Subject Matter Area PG syllabi, Horticultural Sciences)

hero.summary: A two-year research master's on commercial flower production, ornamental plant breeding, nursery management, turf and landscape design. Students combine advanced coursework with a supervised thesis, preparing for research, state horticulture, nursery, landscaping and flower-business careers.

overview.heading: What Floriculture and Landscaping involves
paragraphs: M.Sc. (Horticulture) Floriculture and Landscaping deals with ornamental crops and the design of green spaces. It covers cut flowers such as rose, chrysanthemum and carnation, loose flowers used in local markets, foliage and indoor plants, turf grasses, and the planning of gardens and landscapes. Production under open and protected conditions, flower seed production and value addition, including dry flowers, are also part of the field.

Universities generally base the programme on the ICAR Broad Subject Matter Area (BSMA) PG syllabus for Horticultural Sciences, with their own titles and electives. Students take major courses in floriculture and landscaping, minor and supporting courses from related departments, common courses and a seminar, and complete a thesis. TNAU describes a 70-credit load with 30 credits for thesis research and says its programme follows ICAR guidelines.

Naming differs: the ICAR Horticulture group lists 'Floriculture and Landscaping Architecture', TNAU and Dr YSPUHF advertise 'Floriculture and Landscaping', and some university departments use 'Landscape Architecture'. TNAU offers the programme at Coimbatore and Periyakulam, and Dr YSPUHF at Nauni and Neri.

highlights.label: Credit structure (ICAR BSMA)
highlights.value: 70 credits: major 20, minor 8, supporting 6, common 5, seminar 1, thesis 30

highlights.label: Alternative title
highlights.value: Floriculture and Landscape Architecture (varies by university)

who_should_apply: Horticulture graduates who enjoyed ornamental gardening, nursery and flower crop practicals.
Students with an eye for design who want to apply plant knowledge to gardens, campuses and urban green spaces.
Applicants interested in protected cultivation of cut flowers or in flower seed and planting-material production.
Those planning research or teaching careers, or a nursery, landscaping or floral value-addition business.

curriculum.heading: Courses, research and studio-field work
curriculum.intro: Course lists come from the ICAR BSMA Horticultural Sciences syllabus, but each university sets its own titles, codes and electives, so subject names vary. The areas below are representative of floriculture and landscaping major courses; minor and supporting courses are decided with the advisory committee.

structure.focus: Production, improvement and use of ornamental plants, and landscape planning.
courses: Protected cultivation, seed production and value addition in flower crops

structure.focus: Related subjects chosen to back the thesis.
courses: Plant pathology, entomology or soil science
Intellectual property and its management in agriculture
Agricultural research, research ethics and rural development programmes

practical_learning.name: Thesis research
practical_learning.description: A supervised project on a flower crop, ornamental plant or landscape topic, usually begun after first-year coursework and defended at a final viva voce.

practical_learning.name: Protected structures and nursery work
practical_learning.description: Practicals in polyhouses, shade nets and ornamental nurseries on propagation, crop scheduling and quality management.

practical_learning.name: Landscape design exercises
practical_learning.description: Planning garden and landscape layouts, increasingly with design software where the course includes CAD.

practical_learning.name: Study tours and seminars
practical_learning.description: Visits to flower farms, gardens and research stations, plus seminars, at universities that schedule them.

points: A four-year bachelor's degree in horticulture is the usual qualification; some universities also accept B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. Accepted degrees vary by university and year.
For ICAR AIEEA (PG), the subject is in the Horticulture group; qualifying degrees and minimum OGPA/percentage by category are notified in that year's bulletin.
Final-year students can usually apply provisionally if they complete the degree with required marks by the admission deadline.
University seats carry their own OGPA, domicile and reservation rules, which differ by state.

routes.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
routes.description: National NTA-conducted test for ICAR's share of master's seats in agricultural universities and for ICAR deemed university seats; rank also decides ICAR PG scholarship eligibility.

routes.name: University PG entrance test
routes.description: Universities fill their other seats through their own entrance tests or merit lists; Dr YSPUHF, for example, used PGET scores in the 2023 cycle.

routes.name: Self-financing and other quotas
routes.description: Some universities run self-financing, sports or in-service seats under separate rules in the prospectus.

exams.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
exams.note: Computer-based test with a Horticulture subject paper; pattern and dates change by year.

exams.name: University PG entrance tests
exams.note: Syllabus and weightage vary by university.

steps.title: Check eligibility
steps.text: Compare your degree and OGPA with the ICAR bulletin and target university prospectuses, noting the exact programme title each uses.

steps.title: Register for entrance tests
steps.text: Apply for ICAR AIEEA (PG) through NTA and for chosen universities' PG entrance tests.

steps.title: Attend counselling
steps.text: Use your rank in ICAR online counselling or university counselling to pick the subject and institution.

steps.title: Complete admission
steps.text: Report with original documents and fees at the allotted university within the deadline.

fees.summary: Fees differ between universities and seat categories. Regular seats at state agricultural and horticultural universities are usually cheaper than self-financing seats, ICAR-quota and state-quota fees may differ, and hostel and exam charges are separate. No figures are given because no dated official fee schedule was verified; consult the current prospectus.

careers.heading: Careers in flowers, nurseries and landscapes
careers.intro: Graduates find work in public horticulture, research and the ornamental plant industry, and some set up their own nursery, landscaping or floral businesses. A Ph.D. or national eligibility test opens teaching and research routes. Recruitment rules vary by employer and state, and selection is competitive.

roles.title: Horticulture officer
roles.description: Implements state horticulture schemes, including floriculture and nursery programmes, through the state department.

roles.title: Subject matter specialist (horticulture) at a KVK
roles.description: Runs demonstrations and training for growers, including flower crop production.

roles.title: Landscape horticulturist or garden supervisor
roles.description: Plans and maintains gardens, campuses, parks and turf areas for public bodies or private firms.

roles.title: Nursery or flower farm manager
roles.description: Manages propagation, crop scheduling and quality for ornamental nurseries and cut-flower units.

roles.title: Research fellow or associate
roles.description: Supports funded floriculture research in universities and ICAR institutes.

sectors: Municipal parks and urban greening bodies
public_sector_routes: ICAR ASRB National Eligibility Test (NET) in Floriculture and Landscaping for lecturer/assistant professor eligibility
ICAR ASRB Agricultural Research Service and related scientist recruitment
State public service commission horticulture officer examinations
higher_study: Ph.D. in Floriculture and Landscaping (via ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF (PhD) or university entrance)
Ph.D. in allied horticulture disciplines, subject to university rules

skills: Ornamental plant propagation and nursery management
Landscape and garden planning, including design software
Experimental design, analysis and scientific writing

faqs.question: Who can apply for M.Sc. Floriculture and Landscaping?
faqs.answer: Mainly horticulture graduates; some universities also accept B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. The ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and each prospectus list accepted degrees and minimum OGPA.

faqs.question: Is it the same as Floriculture and Landscape Architecture?
faqs.answer: Broadly yes. The ICAR Horticulture group uses 'Floriculture and Landscaping Architecture', while universities use either 'Floriculture and Landscaping' or 'Landscape Architecture' in the title. Check the exact name in each university's list.

faqs.question: Which entrance exams apply?
faqs.answer: ICAR AIEEA (PG), conducted by NTA, for ICAR-quota and ICAR deemed university seats, and university-level PG entrance tests or merit lists for other seats.

faqs.question: Does the course include landscape design?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ornamental gardening and landscaping is a core area, and the BSMA course areas also cover turf management, interiorscaping and computer-aided landscape design. Coverage depends on the university.

faqs.question: How much research is involved?
faqs.answer: Thesis research carries 30 of the 70 credits in the ICAR BSMA framework and is usually done in the second year under a major adviser.

faqs.question: What careers can I pursue?
faqs.answer: Options include state horticulture posts, KVK roles, landscaping and nursery management, cut-flower farm management, research fellowships and running a floriculture business.

faqs.question: Can I go on to a Ph.D. or teaching?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ph.D. admission is through ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF (PhD) or university tests, and Floriculture and Landscaping is listed as an ASRB NET discipline for assistant professor eligibility.
